(p-٨٧)In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

Surah al-'Asr

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿By the 'Asr (time)﴾ ﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾.

Al-'Asr is a name for time as a whole, or for a part of it. For this reason there is disagreement about what is meant by it, since it is not made clear here.

It was said: it is all of time (al-dahr). God swore by it because of the wonders it contains: a nation passes away and another comes, a decree is carried out, a sign appears, and yet time remains the same and does not change. Night is followed by day, and day is driven off by night, so time is in itself a wonder.

As it has been said: it is something existent that resembles the non-existent, and something moving that resembles the still.

As it has been said:

؎I see time as a ship that carries us toward death, and we do not perceive its motions.

So time is in itself a sign, whether in its past, when one does not know when it began, or in its present, when one does not know how it will pass, or in its future.

This view is supported by what is reported as a statement of 'Ali (may God be pleased with him), and as a raised report (marfu') through an irregular reading (shadhdh): "By the 'Asr and the calamities of time." It is taken as an explanation (tafsir) if it is not sound as Qur'an. This meaning is also reported from Ibn 'Abbas.

On this is based the poet's line:

؎The path of passion is rugged, and the sea of passion is deep ∗∗∗ a day of passion is a month, and a month of passion is an age.

It was also said that al-'Asr means the night and the day.

(p-٨٨)Humayd ibn Thawr said:

؎The two 'asrs did not tarry, a day and a night ∗∗∗ when they sought to reach what they would complete.

The two 'asrs (al-'asran) also mean the morning and the evening.

As it was said:

؎I put him off morning and evening until he tires of me ∗∗∗ and he accepts half the debt while his nose is in the dust.

Matl is procrastination and delaying a debt.

As it was said:

؎Every debtor has paid and satisfied his creditor ∗∗∗ and the one who was put off is mighty, while his creditor is distressed.

It was also said that al-'ashiyy (the late afternoon/evening) is the time from the sun's decline until its setting, and this is the view of al-Hasan and Qatadah.

From it is the poet's saying:

؎Go with us in the afternoon, O 'Amr, for the 'asr has grown short ∗∗∗ and in the first going-forth lie the spoils and the reward.

It is also reported from Qatadah that it is the last hour of the hours of the day, because of the exaltation of oaths made at it, and because He swore by the dawn and the forenoon.

It was said: it is the 'Asr prayer, because it is the middle prayer.

It was said: it is the era of the Prophet (ﷺ) or the time of his community, because it resembles the late afternoon of the life of the world.

What appears, and God Almighty knows best, is that the closest of all these views are two. Either it is general, meaning time (al-dahr), because of the irregular reading, since its lowest rank is that of explanation, and because by its generality it includes the remaining views. Or it is the 'asr of the human being, meaning his lifespan and the duration of his life, which is the place of gain and loss, as the context suggests, and because it concerns the servant himself as admonition and benefit.

This meaning is favored by the surahs that flank this one: al-Takathur before it and al-Humazah after it. The first censures this distraction and rivalry in wealth and children, until the visiting of graves through death, and the place of all that is the life of the human being.

(p-٨٩)Surah al-Humazah is nearly the same in meaning, in ﴿Who collects wealth and counts it﴾ ﴿He thinks that his wealth will make him immortal﴾ [al-Humazah: 2-3].

The gathering of wealth and counting it occur in the life of a human being, and his life is limited, and he is not immortal in this world, just as faith and righteous deeds are tied to the life of a human being.

On this basis, either what is meant by al-'Asr in this surah is the general sense, because it includes everything and because of the irregular reading, and this is the strongest. Or it is the life of the human being, because it is most bound to his deeds, and all the other usages would then be cases of naming the whole while intending a part. And God Almighty knows best.

His saying: ﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾.

The word al-insan, although singular, has "al" which makes it generic.

The Shaykh (may God's mercy be upon us and upon him) explained this in Daf' Iham al-Idtirab (Removing the Apparent Contradiction), and attention has been drawn to it repeatedly. So it includes the Muslim and the disbeliever, except those whom God Almighty exempted.

It was said: it is specific to the disbeliever, but the first is preferable because of the generality.

﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾ is the answer to the oath. As for khusr (loss): it was said it is being cheated, it was said diminution, it was said punishment, and it was said destruction, and all are close.

The root of khusr and khusran, like kufr and kufran, is a decrease from the capital. He does not specify here the kind of loss or in what, but leaves it unrestricted so that it is general, and He used the particle of containment (fi, "in") to indicate that mankind is immersed in loss and that it surrounds him from every side.

If we look at two matters, namely the exception and the surah before it, this generality becomes clear. For the implication of the exception includes four matters: the absence of faith, which is disbelief; the absence of righteous deed, which is corrupt deed; the absence of mutual counsel to truth, which is either the complete absence of mutual counsel or mutual counsel to falsehood; and the absence of mutual counsel to patience, which is either the complete absence of mutual counsel or impatience and panic.

The surah before it speaks of the human being's distraction by rivalry in wealth and children, seeking riches and increase in them, and the opposite of that is the loss of wealth and children, which is loss.

(p-٩٠)Accordingly, the loss is in religion with respect to faith through disbelief; in islam, which is abandoning deeds, though faith in the technical sense includes it; in distraction with falsehood and leaving the truth; and in impatience and panic.

Hence also the abandoning of command and prohibition in what contains the servant's benefit, his success, and the soundness of his religion and worldly life. All of this has evidence in the Qur'an, which we summarize as follows:

As for loss through disbelief, it is as in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿If you associate others with God, your deeds will surely be nullified, and you will surely be among the losers﴾ [al-Zumar: 65].

And His saying: ﴿Those who denied the meeting with God have lost﴾, that is, because they did not work for this meeting, and confined their concern to the life of this world, so they wasted themselves and their share in the Hereafter.

As for loss through abandoning deeds, it is as in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And those whose scales are light, those are the ones who have lost themselves﴾ [al-A'raf: 9], because the scales are the measures of deeds, as has preceded: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it﴾ [al-Zalzalah: 7].

Similar is: ﴿And whoever takes Satan as a protector instead of God has certainly suffered a clear loss﴾ [al-Nisa': 119], because he will be of the party of Satan: ﴿Unquestionably, the party of Satan are the losers﴾ [al-Mujadilah: 19], that is, by their obeying him in disobedience to God.

As for loss through abandoning mutual counsel to truth, after the truth there is nothing but misguidance, and the truth is Islam in its entirety. God Almighty said: ﴿And whoever seeks other than Islam as a religion, it will never be accepted from him, and in the Hereafter he will be among the losers﴾ [Al 'Imran: 85].

As for loss through abandoning mutual counsel to patience and falling into impatience and panic, it is as God Almighty said: ﴿And among the people is he who worships God on an edge: if good befalls him, he is content with it, but if a trial befalls him, he turns back on his face. He has lost this world and the Hereafter. That is the clear loss﴾ [al-Hajj: 11].

Verifying the ground (tahqiq al-manat) concerning the reality of man's loss

They agreed that the capital of the human being in his life is his lifespan. He was charged to employ it during the period of his existence in this world, which is like a marketplace for him. If he employs it in good he profits, and if he employs it in evil he loses.

(p-٩١)This meaning is indicated by His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, God has purchased from the believers their lives and their wealth in exchange for that they will have Paradise﴾ to the end of the verse [al-Tawbah: 111].

And His saying: ﴿Shall I direct you to a transaction that will save you from a painful punishment?﴾ ﴿You believe in God and His Messenger﴾ to the end of the verse [al-Saff: 10-11].

In the hadith in Muslim: "Purification is half of faith."

And at its end: "Every person goes out in the morning and sells himself, either freeing it or destroying it." This confirms that the capital of the human being is his lifespan.

Because of the importance of this lifespan, it is placed as a counterpart to the message and the warning in His saying: ﴿Did We not give you a life long enough for whoever would be reminded to be reminded therein? And the warner came to you﴾ [Fatir: 37].

On this basis they said: God Almighty sent His Messenger with guidance, and guided every human being to the two paths, and made for every human being a station in Paradise and a station in the Fire.

So whoever believes and does righteous deeds, his destination is the station in Paradise and he is spared the station in the Fire; and whoever disbelieves, his destination is the station in the Fire and he abandons his station in Paradise.

As in the hadith of the grave: "The first thing when he enters his grave, if he is a believer, a door to the Fire is opened for him, and it is said to him: that was your seat in the Fire had you not believed. Then it is closed to him, and a door to Paradise is opened for him, and it is said to him: this is your abode on the day the Hour is established. So he says: My Lord, establish the Hour."

If he is a disbeliever, it is exactly the reverse. When the people of Paradise enter Paradise and the people of the Fire enter the Fire, each takes his station in it, and the stations of the people of the Fire in Paradise remain empty and are inherited by the people of Paradise, and the stations of the people of Paradise in the Fire remain empty and are distributed among the people of the Fire. Here the clear loss appears, because whoever leaves a station in Paradise and goes to a station in the Fire is without doubt a loser, and if he leaves his station in Paradise to another and takes in its place another's station in the Fire, that is the clear loss, we seek refuge in God.

As for other than the disbeliever, and the Muslims in general, the loss lies in negligence, such that even if he enters (p-٩٢)Paradise without attaining the highest ranks, he feels the loss for the time in which he was negligent and did not compete in doing good so as to attain the highest ranks.

So this surah is truly a spur to every individual toward earnestness and profitable work. The ranks of Paradise are lofty and its stations high; however much effort a servant expends, there remains before him room for gain and profit. We ask God for success and prosperity.

They have said: No person leaves this world except sorrowful. If he was an evildoer, he grieves over his evildoing, and if he was a doer of good, over his shortcoming. This meaning may be supported by His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is God," and then remain steadfast, the angels descend upon them, saying: Do not fear and do not grieve, but receive good tidings of Paradise, which you were promised﴾ [41:30].

Fear concerns the future that lies ahead of them, and grief concerns the past behind them. And God Almighty knows best.

What shows the gravity of this matter is that when a person is at the end of his life and feels his numbered days and limited hours, and wishes for one more day to take provision from it, or a brief hour to make up for some of what he missed, he cannot find a way to it. So he feels sorrow and grief over the days, nights, months and years that were lost to him without gain or benefit, which could have been profitable for him. In the sound hadith: "There are two blessings in which many people are cheated: health and free time."

That is, they pass by and he does not employ them in the complete avenues of gain, so they are lost to him without any compensation worth mentioning, and then he regrets, when it is no longer the time for regret.

As it was said regarding that:

؎I exchanged a full head of hair for a bare head, and for bright pearly front teeth, small beads,
؎as the Muslim bought when he turned Christian.

A Note

In Surah al-Takathur is the condemnation of distraction by rivalry in wealth, children and the like, then the indication that its cause is ignorance, because if they had known with certain knowledge, that would not have distracted them until death surprised them.

Here too is an indication that the cause of this loss into which man falls is ignorance, which (p-٩٣)drags to disbelief and persistence in falsehood, and hardness of heart and long hopes help in this. As God Almighty said: ﴿Has the time not come for those who believe that their hearts should humble themselves at the remembrance of God and what has come down of the truth, and that they should not be like those who were given the Scripture before, and the term became long for them, so their hearts hardened, and many of them are defiantly disobedient?﴾ [al-Hadid: 16].

Another Note

﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾ states "mankind" explicitly, as has preceded, and another verse has come indicating that the jinn are like humans, in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Those are the ones upon whom the word has come into effect among nations that had passed on before them of the jinn and mankind. Indeed, they were losers﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 18].

The explanation of the jinn's being charged with the call, their responding to it and calling others to it has preceded.

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

(p-٤٦٥)In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

Surah al-'Asr

Statement of the Exalted: ﴿By the declining day (al-'asr)﴾ ﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾.

The apparent meaning of this noble verse indicates that the one of whom it is reported that he is in loss is a single human being, as shown by the singular form of the word "al-insan" (mankind, the human being). Yet the exception made from that one human being, in wording, namely His statement: ﴿Except for those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ [al-'Asr: 3], implies that he is not a single human being.

The answer to this is that the word "al-insan", although singular, carries the definite article "al-" (alif and lam) in the sense of inclusiveness (istighraq, covering all individuals of a kind). Because of it, the singular becomes a form of generality ('umum). On this basis, the meaning of "inna al-insan" is that every human being is in loss, since the inclusive "al-" indicates this.

And Allah, the Exalted, knows best.

The words of the Most High: ﴿Except those who believe, do righteous deeds, enjoin one another to the truth, and enjoin one another to patience.﴾

This is the exception from the "human being" mentioned earlier, which indicated generality, as we have presented before. Faith (iman) in the language means affirmation (tasdiq). In the Shari'ah it means firm conviction in the six pillars of faith, as in the hadith of Jibril (peace be upon him) with the Messenger (ﷺ) when he asked him about Islam, faith and ihsan (excellence).

"And do righteous deeds": the conjunction (al-'atf) implies distinction between the two.

Therefore some people said that deeds are not included in the definition of faith, and their statements are well known.

The majority hold that faith is belief in the heart, utterance with the tongue, and action with the limbs. So action is included in it, and faith increases and decreases. We have already stated that action is closer to being a condition than a part. That is, faith is fulfilled by belief, and its existence does not depend on action; but action is a condition for benefiting from faith, when the servant is able to act. Among the evidence that faith is fulfilled by the definition of belief and utterance, even if the servant was unable to act, is the story of the Companion who accepted Islam at the start of the battle, fought, and was martyred without having prayed a single rak'ah for God, and so entered Paradise.

The majority hold that mere belief does not benefit its holder, just as the Prophet's (ﷺ) uncle believed in the truth of his message but did not say a word with which he (ﷺ) could plead for him. Likewise, if someone believed and uttered the two testimonies but did not act, he would contradict his own statement.

(p-94) We have already presented this issue in detail.

"Righteous deeds" (al-salihat) is the plural of salihah. The Shaykh (may God have mercy on us and on him) previously gave its definition and the conditions for a deed to be righteous, with their evidence: that it accords with the Book of God, that its doer performs it sincerely for the sake of God, that it proceeds from a believer in God, and so on.

His words: ﴿and enjoin one another to the truth﴾.

Mutual enjoining of the truth is considered a case of the specific after the general, because it is included in doing righteous deeds.

It was said: tawasi means that they enjoin one another with the truth.

It was said: the truth is everything opposed to falsehood, so it includes performing acts of obedience and abandoning acts of disobedience.

This was considered one of the foundations of enjoining the good and forbidding the evil, on the strength of the context of enjoining one another to patience, that is, patience in commanding and forbidding, as will come, God willing.

It was said: the truth is the Qur'an, because it includes every command, every prohibition and every good. This is attested by the words of the Most High about the Qur'an: ﴿And with the truth We sent it down, and with the truth it descended﴾ [al-Isra': 105], and His words: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book with the truth, so worship God, devoting the religion to Him alone﴾ [al-Zumar: 2].

Verses in the Qur'an indicate that the counsel to the truth includes the whole Shari'ah, its fundamentals and branches, past and present. Among these is what God enjoined upon the prophets in general, from Nuh and Ibrahim and those after them, in His words: ﴿He has ordained for you of religion what He enjoined upon Nuh, and that which We have revealed to you, and what We enjoined upon Ibrahim, Musa and 'Isa: to establish the religion and not be divided therein﴾ [al-Shura: 13].

Establishing the religion means upholding it in its entirety. This counsel was the practice of the messengers toward their nations and those after them. Ibrahim (peace be upon him) carried it out, as the Most High said: ﴿And Ibrahim enjoined it upon his sons, and so did Ya'qub: "O my sons, God has chosen for you the religion, so do not die except as Muslims."﴾ [al-Baqarah: 132].

After Ibrahim came Ya'qub, as the Most High said: ﴿Or were you witnesses when death approached Ya'qub, when he said to his sons, "What will you worship after me?" They said, "We will worship your God and the God of your fathers, Ibrahim, Isma'il and Ishaq, one God, and to Him we submit."﴾ [al-Baqarah: 133].

(p-95) This is the nations' mutual enjoining of the root of faith and of the Shari'ah in general, and likewise of acts of worship such as prayer and zakah, as in the words of the Most High about the prophet of God 'Isa (peace be upon him): ﴿and He has enjoined upon me prayer and zakah as long as I live﴾ ﴿and to be dutiful to my mother﴾ [Maryam: 31-32].

Likewise the social dimension is evident in the counsel regarding parents and children, for the bonding of the family. Regarding parents there are the words of the Most High: ﴿And We have enjoined upon man concerning his parents: his mother bore him in weakness upon weakness, and his weaning is in two years: be grateful to Me and to your parents; to Me is the final return﴾ ﴿But if they strive with you to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them, but keep them company in this world with kindness﴾ [Luqman: 14-15].

Regarding children He said: ﴿God enjoins you concerning your children: for the male the like of the share of two females﴾ [al-Nisa': 11].

Regarding general rights, with commands and prohibitions, acts of worship and dealings, there came the verses of the Ten Counsels, about which Ibn Mas'ud (may God be pleased with him) said: "Whoever wishes to look at the counsel of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) upon which is his seal, let him recite: ﴿Say: Come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden you: that you associate nothing with Him, and be good to parents, and do not kill your children out of poverty; We provide for you and for them; and do not approach immoralities, what is apparent of them and what is concealed; and do not kill the soul which God has forbidden except by right. That is what He has enjoined upon you, that you may understand﴾ ﴿And do not approach the property of the orphan except in the best way until he reaches maturity; and give full measure and weight with justice; We do not burden any soul except its capacity; and when you speak, be just, even if it concerns a relative; and fulfill the covenant of God. That is what He has enjoined upon you, that you may remember﴾ ﴿And that this is My straight path, so follow it, and do not follow other ways, lest they separate you from His way. That is what He has enjoined upon you, that you may become righteous﴾ [al-An'am: 151-153]."

Those counsels comprise the gateways of good, close the gateways of evil, and are concluded with this clarification and definition: ﴿And that this is My straight path, so follow it, and do not follow other ways﴾.

If we wished to link this with the mutual enjoining of the truth, and link both with al-Fatihah, the result would be as follows regarding His words ﴿and enjoin one another to the truth﴾: a reference to those counsels, which are comprehensive and are titled as being God's straight path.

(p-96) So His words ﴿and enjoin one another to the truth﴾ are as if equivalent to: "and enjoin one another to the straight path, and be steadfast upon it."

Then in Surat al-Fatihah: ﴿Guide us to the straight path﴾ [al-Fatihah: 6], and "this is God's straight path, so follow it."

Thus Surat al-'Asr includes mutual enjoining of steadfastness upon God's straight path and following it. After it comes His statement ﴿and enjoin one another to patience﴾ [al-'Asr: 3], serving as confirmation upon this straight path, since patience is necessary in performing acts of obedience, as it is necessary in abandoning forbidden things.

Those Ten Counsels combined command and prohibition, doing and abandoning. In it there is also an allusion to what the callers to Islam say: that righteous action and calling to the truth and mutually enjoining it involve enjoining the good and forbidding the evil, and whoever undertakes this is generally exposed to people's harm, so they must enjoin one another to patience. So Luqman said to his son, counseling him and combining in his counsel the counsel of Surat al-'Asr: ﴿O my son, establish prayer, enjoin what is good, forbid what is evil, and be patient over what befalls you. Indeed, that is of the matters requiring resolve﴾ [Luqman: 17].

The Shaykh (may God have mercy on us and on him) previously explained in detail the rules of enjoining the good and forbidding the evil at the words of the Most High: ﴿O you who believe, take care of yourselves; those who go astray cannot harm you﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 105], in Surat al-Ma'idah.

So this surah truly became comprehensive of the fundamentals of the message.

As is narrated from al-Shafi'i (may God have mercy on him), he said: "If people reflected on this surah, it would suffice them."

His words ﴿and enjoin one another to the truth﴾: exhortation to mutual enjoining of mercy together with patience also came, in His words: ﴿Then he was of those who believed and enjoined one another to patience and enjoined one another to mercy﴾ [al-Balad: 17].

With these three counsels, namely mutual enjoining of the truth, of patience and of mercy, the constituents of a complete society are perfected, its foundation being the finest virtues and highest values.

For by mutual enjoining of the truth, the truth is established, along with steadfastness upon the straight path.

(p-97) By mutual enjoining of patience, they are able to continue their course on this path and overcome every obstacle facing them.

By mutual enjoining of mercy, they are bound together like a single body. These are gifts that only the Qur'an gave, and it gave them in this brief surah. And success is with God.

A Note

Al-Fakhr al-Razi said: When God the Most High reported of these people that they are saved from loss and win through righteous action and faith, He reported that they were not content with what concerned themselves, but extended to others, calling them to what they themselves had attained, in line with his saying (ﷺ): "Love for your brother what you love for yourself." End, in summary.

This is attested by the words of the Most High: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is God," then remain steadfast, the angels descend upon them﴾ up to His words ﴿And who is better in speech than one who calls to God, does righteousness, and says, "I am among the Muslims"?﴾ ﴿And not equal are the good deed and the evil deed. Repel with that which is better; then behold, the one between whom and you there was enmity will become as though he were a close friend﴾ ﴿But none is granted it except those who are patient, and none is granted it except one of great fortune﴾ [Fussilat: 30-35].

God the Most High has made clear that people are of three kinds in regard to the messengers' call:

A people who believed and said, "Our Lord is God," and remained steadfast upon that through righteous action.

A people whose aspiration rose to calling others, and they are without doubt best in speech.

A people who were hostile to the callers and wronged them.

Then He made clear the callers' stance toward those wrongdoers in the course of His words: ﴿And not equal are the good deed and the evil deed. Repel﴾, that is, the wrongdoers' wrong, ﴿with that which is better﴾, so that they become your friends. He made clear that this station ﴿is granted only to those who are patient﴾, and then that whoever rises to it and follows its path is truly "one of great fortune."

(p-98) A Note

I had heard from the Shaykh (may God have mercy on us and on him) his saying: The callers have two enemies: one from mankind and the other from the devils.

God has guided us to how to overcome both and ward off their evil.

As for the enmity of mankind, it is by meeting evil with good, so that the enemy becomes a close friend.

As for the enemy from the jinn, it is by seeking refuge from him: ﴿And if an evil suggestion from Satan should incite you, then seek refuge in God. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing﴾ [Fussilat: 36].

We ask God the Most High for guidance and success.

We have indicated that the Shaykh (may God have mercy on us and on him) presented the discussion of enjoining the good and forbidding the evil at the words of the Most High: ﴿O you who believe, take care of yourselves; those who go astray cannot harm you when you are guided﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 105].

He mentioned Surat al-'Asr there, and set out several issues on the method of enjoining the good and forbidding the evil, which are indispensable.
